# The net.osmand classes the NATIVE library reaches by name, and therefore the exact
# set R8 must not remove. Nothing here is hand-typed: regenerate with
#
#   grep -rhoE '"net/osmand/[A-Za-z0-9/$_]+"' <core-legacy>/native/src | tr -d '\"' | sort -u
#
# against the core-legacy revision pinned in build-dev.yml (CORE_LEGACY_REF).
#
# Why this file has to exist. -dontobfuscate is set, so R8 cannot rename anything and the
# ONLY failure mode available to it is removal. That makes "did R8 delete something the
# native side needs" a question with a deterministic answer, because R8's -printusage
# writes exactly what it removed. Checking that list against this one turns a
# NoSuchMethodError on a Cairo road into a red build four minutes after the push.
#
# Two of these are NOT greppable from the Java side and would be missed by any
# call-site search: java_wrap.cpp:173-182 does GetObjectClass on an object it is handed
# and reads the fields 'interrupted' (Z) and 'renderedState' (I) off whatever class comes
# back. Line 1230 shows that object is a RenderingContext, so keeping that class with its
# fields covers it - but only because someone went and looked.
#
# Generated 2026-08-06 from CORE_LEGACY_REF=071503e280d77c2a959d3690845f5e56b2c7e4b3
# Count at generation: 35
